constitution_recertification.key_principle: Article XXVIII: hypothesis → evidence → model → validation → conclusion. Each promotion requires NEW evidence. The classifier hypothesis is at HYPOTHESIS stage only. No promotion permitted.

frozen_scientific_claim.canonical_statement: No direct R2-C3 predictor has been demonstrated in open data.
frozen_scientific_claim.classification: FACT — supported by Round 56f predictor hierarchy showing 0 Tier-1 (DIRECT_R2C3) predictors.
what_this_does_NOT_establish: Does NOT establish that R2-C3 is unmeasurable
Does NOT establish that no predictor could ever work
Does NOT establish that the headache-phenotype classifier hypothesis is correct
Does NOT establish that the headache-phenotype classifier hypothesis is incorrect
frozen_scientific_claim.use_rule: This claim may be cited as the current evidence state. It may NOT be cited as evidence that the classifier hypothesis is the correct invention direction.

hypothesis_attack.hypothesis: Pre-treatment headache phenotype (ICHD-3 classification) predicts post-VSS R2-C3 phenotype (headache despite normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis).
hypothesis_attack.attack_question_1: Does baseline headache phenotype actually predict post-VSS phenotype after controlling for baseline ICP, gradient, migraine, BMI, stent type, and disease severity?
hypothesis_attack.answer_1: UNKNOWN — cannot be tested with current open data. No open cohort has both ICHD-3 headache phenotype classification AND post-VSS R2-C3 phenotype classification per-patient. The hypothesis CANNOT be confirmed or refuted at zero cost.
hypothesis_attack.attack_question_2: Does adding venous/CGRP features improve out-of-sample performance materially over headache phenotype alone?
hypothesis_attack.answer_2: UNKNOWN — cannot be tested. No open cohort has headache phenotype + venous manometry + CGRP + VSS outcome in the same patients.

strongest_alternative_explanation_per_ar.alternative: The 34.9% persistent headache rate after VSS (Intrapiromkul 2025) is NOT evidence that a pre-treatment classifier would work. The alternative explanation is that the persistent headache is HETEROGENEOUS — some patients have migraine, some have medication-overuse headache, some have persistent elevated ICP (R2-C1), some have unrecognized restenosis (R2-C2b), and some have true R2-C3. A classifier trained on this heterogeneous outcome (without phenotype labels) would learn noise, not signal.
strongest_alternative_explanation_per_ar.test: Would require per-patient phenotype classification to test whether the 34.9% is homogeneous (classifier could work) or heterogeneous (classifier would fail). Cannot be tested at zero cost.
strongest_alternative_explanation_per_ar.implication: The hypothesis may be WRONG. The 34.9% statistic does NOT establish that pre-treatment selection is the solution. The actual invention could be: better patient selection, a different diagnostic pathway, phenotype-specific treatment, a monitoring system, or nothing at all. We must let the evidence choose.

hypothesis_attack.attack_result: The hypothesis SURVIVES the attack (it is not refuted), but it is NOT CONFIRMED. It remains a DISCOVERY HYPOTHESIS. Per Article XXVIII, no promotion to evidence/model/validation/conclusion is permitted without new evidence.

weak_label_framework.principle: WEAK_LABEL ≠ R2-C3 ground truth. Every weak label must carry explicit noise model and corruption testing requirements.

weak_labels.name: Persistent headache despite patent stent
weak_labels.label_definition: Patient-reported headache at 6+ months post-VSS, with confirmed patent stent on 6-month angiography (no restenosis).
weak_labels.label_noise_model: MIXTURE — this label conflates: (a) true R2-C3 (headache + normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis), (b) R2-C1 (headache + elevated ICP + papilledema recurrence + no restenosis — stent patent but ICP not controlled), (c) R2-C5 (headache + other symptoms, ICP/papilledema status unknown). The proportion of true R2-C3 in this weak label is UNKNOWN.
weak_labels.false_positive_risk: HIGH — a patient classified as WL-1 may have R2-C1 (elevated ICP) rather than R2-C3 (normal ICP). Without ICP measurement, the false positive rate for R2-C3 is unbounded.
weak_labels.false_negative_risk: MODERATE — a patient with true R2-C3 but WITHOUT angiographic confirmation of patent stent would be missed. This could happen if follow-up angiography was not performed or was not routine.
weak_labels.corruption_testing_requirement: Any model trained on WL-1 must be tested under label corruption: (a) randomly flip 20% of labels, (b) measure performance degradation, (c) if degradation is severe, the model is learning label-specific noise, not signal. (d) Also test with simulated R2-C1 contamination: assume 30% of WL-1 positives are actually R2-C1, re-train, measure performance change.
weak_labels.defensibility: LOW for R2-C3 specifically. MODERATE for 'persistent headache after VSS' as a broader outcome.

weak_labels.name: Persistent headache + no repeat intervention
weak_labels.label_definition: ICD-10 R51 (headache) present at 1+ year post-VSS, with NO repeat CPT 37238/37239/1009323 (no re-stenting or shunt).
weak_labels.label_noise_model: HIGH NOISE — TriNetX EHR data lacks ICP, papilledema grade, and angiographic restenosis data. The 'no repeat intervention' is a proxy for 'no symptomatic restenosis requiring treatment' but does NOT rule out asymptomatic restenosis. The headache could be: R2-C3, R2-C1 (if ICP elevated but no intervention offered), R2-C5 (other symptoms), or even unrelated to IIH.
weak_labels.false_positive_risk: VERY HIGH — without any physiological measurements, the false positive rate for R2-C3 is unbounded. A patient with elevated ICP who was offered but declined shunt would be classified as WL-2.
weak_labels.false_negative_risk: HIGH — patients with R2-C3 who had repeat intervention for OTHER reasons (e.g., stent for a different venous segment) would be excluded.
weak_labels.corruption_testing_requirement: WL-2 is too noisy for meaningful corruption testing. Recommend: do NOT use WL-2 for any model training. Use only for GROUP-LEVEL descriptive statistics.
weak_labels.defensibility: VERY LOW for R2-C3. Acceptable only for population-level descriptive epidemiology.

weak_labels.name: Headache despite normal pressures (Ahmed definition)
weak_labels.label_definition: Persistent headache post-VSS with documented normal pressures (LP or continuous ICP monitoring showing normal ICP).
weak_labels.label_noise_model: LOW NOISE — Ahmed 2011 confirmed ALL FOUR R2-C3 components for 3 cases: headache + normal ICP (Rickham reservoir) + resolved papilledema + no restenosis. This is GROUND TRUTH, not a weak label.
weak_labels.false_positive_risk: ZERO for the 3 Ahmed cases (all 4 components confirmed).
weak_labels.false_negative_risk: LOW for the 3 Ahmed cases (explicitly described as having persistent headache).
weak_labels.corruption_testing_requirement: Not needed — these are ground truth labels. But n=3 is too small for model training.
weak_labels.defensibility: HIGH — these are GROUND TRUTH R2-C3 cases, not weak labels.
weak_labels.reclassification: WL-3 should be reclassified as GROUND_TRUTH, not WEAK_LABEL. The weak label framework applies to WL-1 and WL-2 only.

weak_label_use_rules: 1. Any model trained on WEAK_LABELS must report performance under label corruption (20% random flip).
2. Any model trained on WEAK_LABELS must report sensitivity to R2-C1 contamination (assume 30% of positives are R2-C1).
3. WEAK_LABEL results may NOT be reported as R2-C3 prevalence or R2-C3 prediction accuracy. They must be reported as 'WL-X accuracy' with explicit noise caveats.
4. GROUND_TRUTH (Ahmed n=3) may be used for validation only, not training (too small).
5. Any claim of 'R2-C3 predictor' requires GROUND_TRUTH validation, not WEAK_LABEL validation.

prior_art_attack.hypothesis_under_attack: Pre-treatment headache phenotype classifier for VSS response

most_relevant_prior_art.title: Predicting the need for retreatment in venous sinus stenting for idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
most_relevant_prior_art.what_they_did: Logistic regression: OP + age + sex + BMI → VSS retreatment (binary failure)
most_relevant_prior_art.what_they_found: OP predicts failure (OR=1.064, p=0.039) but POOR discrimination
what_they_did_NOT_do: Did NOT distinguish failure phenotypes (R2-C1 vs R2-C2 vs R2-C3)
Did NOT use CGRP or venous pressure distribution
most_relevant_prior_art.explicit_acknowledgment: 'Identifying which patients are likely to benefit most, and which are likely to require repeat procedures, is currently unclear.' — Calls for 'further studies'
most_relevant_prior_art.anticipates_hypothesis: PARTIALLY — anticipates the PROBLEM (predicting VSS response) but NOT the APPROACH (headache phenotype classifier) or the TARGET (R2-C3 specifically)

most_relevant_prior_art.title: Predictors for venous sinus stent retreatment in patients with IIH
most_relevant_prior_art.what_they_did: Identified BMI as statistically significant predictor for recurrent symptoms after VSS
most_relevant_prior_art.anticipates_hypothesis: PARTIALLY — anticipates the general approach (find predictors of VSS failure) but NOT the specific classifier

most_relevant_prior_art.title: Risk factors for failed transverse sinus stenting in pseudotumor cerebri patients
most_relevant_prior_art.what_they_did: Compared 15 successes vs 3 failures; found OP 50 vs 37 cmH2O (p<0.05)
most_relevant_prior_art.anticipates_hypothesis: PARTIALLY — same problem, different predictor (OP only)

most_relevant_prior_art.title: Post-intervention pressure gradient as predictor of 6-month clinical outcome
most_relevant_prior_art.what_they_did: Used POST-treatment gradient to predict outcome
most_relevant_prior_art.anticipates_hypothesis: NO — this is post-treatment, not pre-treatment. Different clinical decision point.

most_relevant_prior_art.title: Dural Venous Sinus Stent in Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
most_relevant_prior_art.what_they_will_do: 'Identify clinical determinants and factors that predict outcome including primary outcome and secondary outcome'
most_relevant_prior_art.anticipates_hypothesis: UNKNOWN — trial not yet started. May or may not use headache phenotype. Primary outcomes: HIT-6 (headache impact), Frisén grade (papilledema), perimetry, tinnitus. If they collect ICHD-3 headache phenotype as a baseline variable, they MAY partially anticipate the hypothesis.

gap_analysis.problem_recognized: YES — Kahan 2021 explicitly states the problem is 'currently unclear' and calls for 'further studies'
gap_analysis.approach_established: PARTIALLY — logistic regression on baseline variables is established (Kahan, El Mekabaty, Goodwin). But NO study uses headache phenotype (ICHD-3) as a predictor.
gap_analysis.target_distinguished: NO — no prior study distinguishes R2-C3 from other failure phenotypes. All use binary success/failure or retreatment need.
gap_analysis.specific_combination_absent: YES — the specific combination of [headache phenotype + venous manometry + R2-C3 target] is NOT described in any open publication.
gap_analysis.but: The absence of a published combination does NOT mean it would work. It means it hasn't been tried. Per Article XXI (discovery evidence is not search activity), zero results is not novelty.

attack_result.hypothesis_survives_prior_art: YES — the specific combination is not anticipated by prior art
attack_result.hypothesis_survives_because: No prior study uses ICHD-3 headache phenotype as a predictor of VSS response, and no prior study targets R2-C3 specifically
attack_result.but_survival_is_NOT_evidence: Per Article XXVIII, survival of prior-art attack is PERMISSION TO SEEK EVIDENCE, not evidence of invention. The hypothesis remains at DISCOVERY_HYPOTHESIS stage.
attack_result.strongest_alternative: The alternative explanation is that headache phenotype does NOT predict VSS response after controlling for confounders. This cannot be tested at zero cost.
attack_result.next_attack: Search for any patent or patent application that claims a method for selecting IIH patients for VSS based on headache phenotype. If found, the hypothesis may be anticipated by patent art (not just literature).
